content: All editable pages on WikiDoc have an associated page history, which provides a detailed record of all changes made to the page in reverse-chronological order. This is also referred to as the revision history or edit history. To view a specific version of a page, you can click on the corresponding date in the page history. If you wish to compare an older version with the current version, you can click on the cur link. To compare a version with its immediate predecessor, click on the last link. For comparing two specific versions, select the radio button in the right column for the newer version and the left column for the older version, then click the Compare selected versions button. Minor edits are marked with an m for easy identification. The page history contains the old versions of the wikitext, along with a record of the date and time (in UTC) of each edit, the username or IP address of the contributor, and their edit summary. You can access the page history by clicking the history tab at the top of the page. In the page history, edits are displayed from the newest to the oldest. Each edit is listed on a single line, showing the time and date, the contributor's name or IP address, the edit summary, and other diagnostic information. The history tab is highlighted when viewing the page history. Links allow navigation to the user's most recent edits, oldest edits, or the next/previous page of edits. The number of edits displayed per page can be adjusted (e.g., 20, 50, 100, 250, or 500), with higher numbers increasing the page length but reducing the number of pages. The cur link directs you to a diff page showing the differences between a specific edit and the current version. The current revision is displayed below the changes, allowing you to see how the page is currently rendered. The last link shows the differences between a specific edit and its previous version, with the most recent version displayed below the changes. Two columns of radio buttons allow you to select any two versions for comparison. For example, to compare versions 10 and 11, click the left radio button next to version 11, then the right radio button next to version 10, and finally click Compare selected versions. This will display a diff page showing the changes between the two versions, with the most recent version (in this case, version 10) displayed below the changes. The page history also provides the time and date of each edit in local time, based on the user's preference settings. The username or IP address of the contributor is displayed, along with the edit summary, which is the text entered by the user in the edit summary box. If the user edited only a section of the page, the edit summary begins with an arrow link and gray text indicating the section name. This text is automatically added when editing a section. Minor edits, marked with m, indicate small corrections to the page. If the move page feature has been used to rename a page, the entire edit history of the article, both before and after the move, is preserved. The old title becomes a redirect and loses its edit history. After merging two pages, one typically becomes a redirect, and its revision history is retained. Edits made to deleted pages are not retained in the contributor's User Contributions pages, but the revision history can be retrieved by an administrator, who can also undelete the page. If you are dissatisfied with recent edits to a page, you can revert the page to any previous version. A section of a page may be an included separate page via a method called transclusion. In such cases, a separate edit history is maintained for the transcluded page, which must be watched separately. An image (or any uploaded file) can be replaced by uploading a new file with the same name. All versions of the image are retained in the image history, which is part of the image description page. Deleted images are not retained, and it is not possible to undelete an image. The only record available for deleted images is the upload log, deletion log, and possibly the votes for deletion archive. It is sometimes useful to link to a specific version of an article, such as when referencing a particular version for review. The URL of the old version can be obtained from the browser's location bar and used for permanent reference. The history of the wikitext should not be confused with the history of the rendered page, as templates and images may vary over time. The current versions of templates and images are used unless old versions are given different names. Special:Export allows the creation of an XML file containing the wikitext of the current and optionally all old versions of specified pages, along with the date, time, username, and edit summary. This feature also enables searching for text across all versions of specified pages. Archiving texts in separate pages is preferable to using the page history as an archive, as texts in archive pages can be found by search engines. Page histories can only be searched after applying Special:Export. An index of old versions of a page, with links to them, can be prepared. When viewing the history of a watched page directly, the most recent edit may be marked with an update marker (updated since my last visit) if the edit was made by someone else and you have not viewed the page since the edit was made. However, not all unseen edits are marked, and the positioning of the message may be misleading.
